0100.name: Game mode
desc: Master state of the game: the main loop runs one routine per frame chosen by this value (via $009322).
Modes step forward with INC $0100 as each stage (fade, load, wait) finishes; some routines set it directly.
Values: $00 = load Nintendo Presents, $01 = Nintendo Presents, $02 = fade to title, $07 = title/demo,
$08 = file select, $09 = erase file, $0B = fade out to overworld, $0C = load overworld, $0F/$10 = Mario Start,
$11 = Mario Start text and level music, $14 = in level, $18 = reload cutscene, $25/$26 = ending, fade to
THE END.

0101.name: Loaded sprite GFX files
desc: Remembers which sprite graphics file is currently loaded in each of the 4 sprite GFX slots in VRAM.
The upload routine compares the wanted file to this entry and skips the upload when it is already loaded,
then stores the new file number. Set to $FF at game start so the first level uploads everything.
Values: $FF = nothing loaded.

0105.name: Loaded FG/BG GFX files
desc: Same caching idea as $0101, but for the foreground/background graphics file slots. The FG/BG upload
routine skips a file that is already loaded and stores the new file number after uploading.
A routine also fills the table with $80, which marks the slot as needing a fresh upload.
Values: $80 = slot not valid/forces reload.

0109.name: Intro level override
desc: Non-zero makes the game load a level directly instead of using the overworld. Set to $E9 when the title
screen demo starts the intro level; $E9 - $24 = $C5 is the level number used. The Mario Start mode picks
intro level music when it is $E9, the overworld loader skips the map when it is non-zero, and the message
box and level loader test it to behave differently in the intro. Cleared at reset, by the message box
close routine and by file select, which means normal overworld play.
Values: 0 = normal, $E9 = intro level.

0200.name: OAM entry 0 X position
0200.kind: byte, shadow OAM (sprite 0; indexed by OAM offset X or Y)
desc: Shadow copy of the X position of hardware sprite 0. Shadow OAM ($0200-$041F) is DMA'd to the PPU every frame.
Each sprite is 4 bytes: X, Y, tile, properties. Game code picks a free slot and writes all four.
Drawing routines (sprites, smoke, score, cutscenes) write it; the NMI DMA is the only reader. Slot 0 is
also used by the item box drawing.
Values: screen X in pixels, $00-$FF (the high X bit lives in the $0400 table).

Values: screen Y in pixels; $F0 hides the sprite (off-screen).
